inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 102.974m shares outstanding at 20 Oct 2026 (FY2026 10-K cover) plus ~1.2m dilutive RSU/option shares (Q4 FY2026 diluted less basic weighted average: 398/3.76 vs 398/3.80). Held FLAT because SBC and the cash tax withheld on vesting are fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count. The 1.5m shares bought between 31 Aug and 20 Oct 2026 are in this count, so the US$542m paid for them is deducted in equity_bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: 'Recognition of stock-based compensation expense and related charges' 140 plus financing-activity 'Treasury stock minimum tax withholding related to vesting of restricted stock' 67. Jabil publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-yr UST), ERP ~5%, beta ~1.2 gives cost of equity ~10.3%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (senior notes 3.0-5.45%), debt ~12% of capital, giving ~9.5%. One WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality and customer concentration are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP filer. Operating leases: the US$126m straight-line cost is already inside operating income and EBITDA, so the US$641m operating lease liability is EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are treated as debt: the US$319m finance lease liability (88 current + 231 non-current) is INCLUDED in total_debt, principal payments are not deducted from the flows, and the assets they fund (US$208m of finance-lease additions in FY2026, 136 in FY2025) are charged through capex_pct_path on top of net cash capex.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are US$4m of equity; immaterial, no adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (Drivers route), with the cyclical/lease adaptations. Jabil is a contract electronics manufacturer whose value is an operating cash-flow stream; no bank/REIT/holdco features. FRESH BUILD, no prior valuation. OWNER FCF: reported FCF 1,374 (OCF 2,002 less gross capex 628; the company's 'adjusted FCF' of 1,532 nets 158 of PP&E sale proceeds) less SBC plus vesting-tax withholding 207 = 1,167. Interest income not stripped: Jabil is in net debt. EBITDA BASIS: ebitda_margin_path is core operating income plus depreciation (ex acquired-intangible amortisation) LESS recurring restructuring and deal costs. FY2026: core operating income 2,069 + depreciation 592 = 2,661, less restructuring 97 and acquisition charges 34 = 2,530, or 7.04% of revenue. Restructuring is charged because it has recurred every year (97 / 181 / 296 in FY2026/25/24); the company's core measures exclude it. D&A of 681 (1.89%) includes 89 of intangible amortisation, kept in for the tax shield and added back. CASH TAX: 351 paid in FY2026 after ~268 of interest and receivable-sale losses; grossed up for that shield it is ~24-25% of model EBIT, so the unlevered path starts at 24%. RECEIVABLE SALES: US$1,055m of sold-and-uncollected receivables (677 trade AR sale programs + 378 securitisation) is treated as debt in equity_bridge, because its financing cost (79 loss on sale, booked in other expense) sits outside the core operating income the flows are built from. WORKING CAPITAL: net operating working capital is negative (~-1.3bn: payables and accruals of 21.1bn exceed receivables, contract assets, inventory and prepaids of 19.8bn) and was flat through a 6.2bn revenue increase, so base capture is 0 rather than the negative capture usual for a manufacturer. BUYBACKS: 1,060 spent in FY2026 against 207 of SBC and withholding, so the flat count is more than funded. GUIDANCE: FY2027 revenue ~44.5bn, core operating margin ~6.1%, core EPS 17.55 and adjusted FCF ~1.6bn, as recorded in JBL_Analysis.json (guidance block, as of the 30 Sep 2026 Q4 release). The release itself (8-K) is not in Extracted/ and was not read first-hand; the 10-K independently confirms only the FY2027 net capex guide of 1.5-2.0% of revenue and the Q4 FY2026 run-rate (10,616, +29% y/y). Base year 1 is the guide; the base-case year-1 unlevered owner FCF of ~1.5bn squares with the 1.6bn adjusted-FCF guide once SBC, vesting-tax withholding and finance-lease additions are charged and after-tax interest is added back.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (-5.4% over 5 years) because buybacks of US$6.2bn over FY2021-26 exceeded retained earnings; it diverges far more than 30% from revenue and EPS and is unusable as a growth anchor. EPS growth is buyback- and margin-driven (diluted shares 152m to 107m). Revenue 5-year CAGR is used as the long-run anchor instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less vesting-tax withholding): FY2021 150, FY2023 573, FY2026 1,167. The FY2021 base is depressed by working-capital build, so the 5-year figure is not a trend. Owner-FCF growth is slightly ahead of reported, so SBC is not outgrowing cash flow. Revenue CAGRs are understated by the FY2024 sale of the Mobility business (~US$2.1bn proceeds).

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 is management's FY2027 revenue guide of ~US$44.5bn (+23.8%), given with Q4 FY2026 results on 30 Sep 2026 and weighted ~45/55 to the second half. Years 2-4 fade hard as the cloud build-out matures off a much larger base; then roughly the 5-year revenue CAGR (4.2%) fading to 2.5%.
base.margin_rationale: Guided FY2027 core operating margin of ~6.1% (5.8% in FY2026), plus depreciation ex intangible amortisation (~1.5% of the larger revenue base), less recurring restructuring and deal costs (~0.3%) = ~7.3%. Held flat: Intelligent Infrastructure earns 6.0% segment margin against 5.5-5.6% elsewhere, but much of its growth is low-margin, consignment-heavy rack integration, so no further mix uplift is assumed.
base.capex_note: Net cash capex at the 1.5-2.0% FY2027 guide (1.75%) plus ~0.4% of finance-lease-funded additions, easing to 2.0%.
base.tax_note: Unlevered cash rate; tax incentives in Malaysia, Singapore, Vietnam, Brazil and Israel expire through FY2030 and the 15% global minimum tax is phasing in.

bear.wc_note: Positive capture here is deliberate and is a COST in this scenario: Jabil's working capital is net negative (customer- and supplier-funded), so a revenue decline unwinds payables faster than inventory and receivables and consumes cash.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands on management's guide (~US$44.5bn revenue, ~6.1% core operating margin) as AI infrastructure demand keeps ramping, then growth normalises sharply as hyperscaler capex growth slows; Intelligent Infrastructure settles at over half of revenue, Regulated Industries (auto, healthcare, energy) grows low-single digits and Intelligent Devices and Robotics (formerly Connected Living) is flat. EBITDA margin holds at ~7.3% (the guided core margin less the restructuring Jabil books every year). The Pii FDA warning letter is remediated at modest cost. Buybacks keep the share count flat-to-down, funded from free cash flow. Revenue reaches ~US$61bn in FY2036 at a ~3.5% owner-FCF margin.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI data-centre build-out runs several more years and Jabil gains share of rack integration, liquid cooling (Mikros) and critical power (Hanley): FY2027 beats the guide and revenue passes US$60bn by FY2029. Mix shifts toward design-led and power/cooling content rather than pass-through assembly, lifting EBITDA margin to ~7.8% (core operating margin ~6.5%), and Customer A's 20% share is diluted by other hyperscalers rather than lost. Regulated Industries recovers with EV and medical-device programmes and the Pii site returns to production.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2027 falls short of a back-half-weighted guide, then hyperscaler capex is digested: Customer A (20% of revenue, in Intelligent Infrastructure) cuts or dual-sources, and revenue falls about 22% over FY2028-29, as it has in past EMS downcycles. Fixed-cost absorption on newly added capacity and a fresh restructuring round take EBITDA margin to ~6%, recovering only to 6.5%. The negative working-capital position unwinds and consumes cash on the way down, tax incentives roll off, and the Pii remediation drags. The business stays solvent and cash-generative (no scenario hits the zero terminal floor) but is valued as the low-margin cyclical it was before FY2024.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: FY2026 growth came almost entirely from one segment, one customer rose to 20% of revenue, and FY2027 is guided up another 24% at what may be a peak in AI infrastructure spending. Base 50%: it takes the guide at face value for one year and assumes no margin gain beyond it. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs both a multi-year extension of hyperscaler capex and a mix-led margin step-up, two things that have to go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Jabil is valued as a low-margin, working-capital-heavy contract manufacturer whose cash flows are cyclical and customer-concentrated, on strict owner FCF: SBC and vesting-tax withholding expensed, recurring restructuring charged, finance leases and sold receivables counted as debt, terminal value capped at 14x FCF (12x in the bear). The gap between this and the market price is mostly the multiple the market is willing to pay for AI-infrastructure growth; the house model does not capitalise peak-cycle growth or core (pre-restructuring, pre-SBC) earnings.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY2027 guidance (~US$44.5bn revenue, ~6.1% core margin) is taken from JBL_Analysis.json, not read first-hand from the earnings release; it is second-half weighted, so most of the guided growth is still to be delivered
Customer A is 20% of revenue and the top five are 37%; a single programme decision moves revenue by billions
AI data-centre capex cycle: FY2026 Intelligent Infrastructure revenue rose 45%, and the bear case assumes only a partial reversal
Working capital is net negative and financed by payables, customer consignment and US$1.1bn of receivable sales; a downturn or tighter supplier terms would consume cash
Sold receivables are treated as debt (about US$10/share); a reader who treats them as true sales would add that back
Restructuring is treated as recurring (about 0.3% of revenue); if it genuinely ends, margins are ~0.3pp higher than modelled
FDA warning letter at the Pii aseptic-fill site (August 2026); manufacturing is paused there
Tax incentives expire through FY2030 and the global minimum tax is being adopted unevenly
